classification_definitions.Genesis blocker: A required capability, dependency, security control, or operational guarantee that is absent or demonstrably defective.
classification_definitions.Qualification gap: An implemented capability that lacks sufficient evidence, testing, or verification.
classification_definitions.Integration gap: A missing or incomplete connection to an independently required Genesis component.
classification_definitions.Documentation gap: Missing, inaccurate, obsolete, or incomplete documentation.
classification_definitions.Operational risk: An infrastructure, reliability, performance, or recovery concern requiring qualification.
classification_definitions.Post-Genesis enhancement: A desirable capability that is not required for the agreed Genesis scope.

findings.title: Governance display scope is unresolved
findings.description: The frozen Genesis application purpose includes governance, while the dedicated Explorer Genesis profile does not include a governance view in requiredViews.
evidence: EXP-CAP-019 is classified scope_decision_required and no Explorer governance API/view was established.
findings.root_cause: Two authoritative scope descriptions use different levels of specificity and no explicit decision reconciles them.
consequences: Final Genesis scope cannot be frozen defensibly while the conflict remains.
Implementing or omitting governance display without a decision could either expand scope silently or miss an intended requirement.
remediation: Record an explicit decision stating whether governance display is required for Explorer Genesis.
Update the dedicated profile and capability/workflow matrices consistently if the decision changes required scope.
tests: fail-closed scope verifier must detect any profile/matrix drift
findings.blocking_rationale: Blocks final scope/qualification closeout, not because governance display is already proven mandatory, but because Genesis requirements may not remain ambiguous.

findings.title: 420Indexer has no qualified deployed testnet endpoint
findings.description: Indexer source and CI are implemented/tested, but its readiness fixture still uses URL REPLACE and PENDING_TESTNET_DEPLOYMENT.
evidence: EXP-DEP-001: source implemented_and_tested; deployment pending_deployment; live qualification unverified.
findings.root_cause: Deployment-stage work has not supplied a real testnet service endpoint and live witness evidence.
consequences: Explorer cannot prove that all 13 required Indexer routes and providers are available on the target network.
Accurate live chain/finality/Registry/consensus presentation cannot be established.
remediation: Deploy the qualified Indexer API on the target testnet.
Publish the endpoint in authoritative runtime configuration/readiness evidence.
Exercise all Explorer-required routes with representative data.
findings.blocking_rationale: The shared Indexer is mandatory for every core Explorer data path; source CI cannot substitute for deployed service qualification.

findings.title: Explorer backend and frontend are not deployed or live-qualified
findings.description: Explorer backend/frontend readiness records still use placeholder URLs and pending deployment status despite implemented source.
evidence: EXP-DEP-002 and EXP-DEP-003 remain pending_deployment/live unverified.
findings.root_cause: Production-equivalent testnet deployment and end-to-end qualification have not been completed.
consequences: Genesis-required workflows cannot be demonstrated through the actual deployed application.
Configuration, routing, browser presentation and failure handling remain unproven in deployment.
remediation: Deploy Explorer backend and frontend to production-equivalent testnet endpoints.
Replace readiness placeholders with authoritative URLs only after deployment evidence exists.
Run the live validator with concrete witnesses.
tests: required-view navigation and API tests against deployed URLs
findings.blocking_rationale: A Genesis user application cannot be qualified solely from local source/CI when its required deployed workflows remain unexecuted.

findings.title: Canonical testnet RPC/node binding is unverified
findings.description: Indexer source supports chain ID 420, wrong-chain rejection and canonical/finality tracking, but the official runtime RPC/node source has not been identified and live-qualified in the Explorer evidence.
evidence: EXP-DEP-004: source implemented; deployment and live qualification unverified.
findings.root_cause: No authoritative target-network runtime binding/evidence is present in the audited Explorer readiness chain.
consequences: A deployed Indexer could be pointed at the wrong or incomplete network source.
Chain identity, finality and canonical data correspondence cannot be demonstrated end-to-end.
remediation: Bind Indexer to the approved testnet RPC/node source.
Record chain ID, endpoint identity and supported canonical/finality methods.
Preserve wrong-chain fail-closed behavior.
findings.blocking_rationale: Accurate Explorer data depends on a qualified canonical upstream; implementation of an RPC adapter is insufficient evidence of correct deployed binding.

findings.title: ProtocolRegistry live deployment and publication are unverified
findings.description: ProtocolRegistry source and frozen address authority exist, but Explorer qualification does not yet prove target-network runtime code or authorized service publications at the frozen address.
evidence: EXP-DEP-005: implemented source; deployment/live qualification unverified.
findings.root_cause: Frozen address configuration has not yet been paired with target-network bytecode, code-hash and publication evidence.
consequences: Protocol service/version views could show stale or incomplete projection data.
Explorer cannot prove that displayed application implementations correspond to canonical Registry state.
remediation: Verify code at 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000434 on the target network.
Record runtime code hash and Registry version/publication evidence.
Cross-check direct canonical reads against Indexer projections.
findings.blocking_rationale: Protocol service/version is a mandatory Genesis view and its canonical Registry dependency must be operational and correct.

findings.title: Registry ABI/descriptor runtime provenance is not qualified
findings.description: Registry/event source definitions exist, but the artifact-backed descriptor build and live historical/version decoding seam are not qualified against deployed Registry provenance.
evidence: EXP-DEP-007 remains source_present/live unverified; EXP-0.1.3 explicitly defers artifact-backed descriptor and live Registry event provenance.
findings.root_cause: Build-time ABI/descriptor inputs and runtime Registry event provenance have not been bound into release evidence.
consequences: Decoded service/version or protocol metadata could be incomplete or mismatched to deployed code.
Historical decoding cannot yet be trusted as release-qualified.
remediation: Produce and pin required ABI/descriptor artifacts for the release path.
Bind descriptors to deployed Registry/runtime hashes and service versions.
Record historical version decoding evidence.
tests: historical version/deprecation decoding against target network
findings.blocking_rationale: Required protocol service/version presentation depends on correct Registry-version decoding and provenance.

findings.title: Deployed consensus/validator provider wiring is unverified
findings.description: Consensus interfaces and views exist in source, but the audited deployment evidence does not prove that the live Indexer server wires a consensus provider with representative validator/epoch/rotation data.
evidence: EXP-DEP-008: implemented source; deployment/live qualification unverified.
findings.root_cause: Source route/interface existence has not been paired with deployed backend/provider composition evidence.
consequences: Mandatory validator and epoch/rotation views may be unavailable or empty despite source-level route coverage.
remediation: Wire and deploy the Indexer consensus provider.
Demonstrate populated consensus responses and Explorer rendering on target testnet.
findings.blocking_rationale: Validator and epoch/rotation are explicitly mandatory Genesis views.

findings.title: Actual transaction fee inspection is incomplete
findings.description: The transaction workflow exposes gasUsed but not effective gas price or a computed actual native fee.
findings.root_cause: The inspected transaction/receipt presentation model lacks the effective gas-price/fee inputs required to calculate the actual fee.
consequences: Users cannot verify the actual cost of a transaction from Explorer.
The transaction-inspection workflow described by the audit is incomplete.
prerequisite_work: define authoritative fee fields for the 420 execution model
remediation: Expose the appropriate effective gas price or authoritative fee value through Indexer/Explorer models.
Render gas used and actual fee distinctly.
tests: known gasUsed × effectiveGasPrice vector or protocol-equivalent fee vector
findings.blocking_rationale: EXP-0.2.2 records fee inspection as a required workflow with an implementation gap, so the workflow cannot be qualified until the missing fee data is implemented.

findings.title: Historical validator-produced block attribution is absent
findings.description: The current block record lacks proposer/validator identity, and Explorer cannot trace a historical block to the validator/proposer that produced it.
findings.root_cause: Historical block provenance and consensus status are modeled separately without a block-to-producer field/mapping in the inspected path.
consequences: Users cannot verify block production attribution through the required validator/block workflow.
prerequisite_work: define authoritative historical producer identity source
remediation: Add historical producer/proposer provenance to the Indexer model/API.
Expose and link producer identity in Explorer block/consensus views.
tests: testnet comparison with canonical consensus data
findings.blocking_rationale: The user-workflow matrix explicitly marks validator-produced block inspection as an implementation gap tied to mandatory block and validator capabilities.

findings.title: Raw contract event inspection is incomplete in the user interface
findings.description: The current event presentation exposes log provenance and topic count but does not present full topic values and log data needed for complete raw event inspection.
evidence: EXP-WF-013 is partial_source; its limitations state that the web table does not display topic values/data.
findings.root_cause: The frontend renders a summarized log table rather than the complete indexed log payload.
consequences: Users cannot independently inspect the full raw event payload through the current Explorer UI.
ABI-decoded semantics cannot be validated against visible raw topics/data.
prerequisite_work: none beyond existing raw log DTO availability
remediation: Render full log topics and data in transaction/block event views with safe formatting and navigation.
Keep ABI-decoded labels secondary to raw provenance.
tests: raw UI values compared with API/indexed record
findings.blocking_rationale: Receipt/logs is a mandatory Genesis view and EXP-0.2.2 identifies event inspection as only partially implemented.

findings.title: Production-equivalent recovery and degraded-state behavior remain unqualified
findings.description: Source tests cover Indexer recovery/reorg/finality behavior, but the Explorer audit has no production-equivalent runtime evidence for restart, upstream outage, indexing delay, incomplete synchronization, or live reorg handling.
evidence: EXP-0.2.4 keeps all mandatory runtime dependencies live-unverified; the audit requires deployment-stage resilience evidence distinct from source tests.
findings.root_cause: No qualified production-equivalent Explorer/Indexer deployment exists yet on which to execute operational recovery scenarios.
consequences: Stale or incomplete data could be served incorrectly under real outages/restarts if deployment behavior diverges from source-level tests.
remediation: Execute restart/resume, RPC outage, stale-data, provider failure and bounded reorg scenarios against deployed services.
Record recovery time, status/finality presentation and fail-closed behavior.
findings.blocking_rationale: Operational consistency and recoverability are explicit Genesis acceptance requirements; existing unit/integration CI is not deployment evidence.

findings.title: Staking/reward-specific Explorer activity view is not implemented
findings.description: No dedicated staking/reward activity route or view was observed.
evidence: EXP-WF-012 is not_observed; the dedicated Genesis profile does not list staking/reward history as a requiredView.
findings.root_cause: The agreed core Explorer profile focuses on validator/epoch/rotation status rather than staking/reward history.
consequences: Users cannot inspect staking/reward history as a first-class Explorer workflow.
dependencies: Indexer staking/reward projection if later added
remediation: If prioritized post-Genesis, define canonical staking/reward data model and add Indexer/API/UI support.
findings.blocking_rationale: Not present in the dedicated Genesis requiredViews; the audit explicitly says optional ecosystem capabilities must not automatically block Genesis.

findings.title: Names and Identity label enrichments are absent
findings.description: No direct 420 Names or 420 Identity label lookup path was established for Explorer.
evidence: EXP-CAP-013 and EXP-CAP-014 are optional_display_enrichment; EXP-DEP-009 and EXP-DEP-010 are not required for Genesis.
findings.root_cause: The dedicated profile intentionally classifies these integrations as optional presentation enrichment.
consequences: Raw addresses remain less human-readable but retain complete canonical provenance.
prerequisite_work: qualified owning protocols if later enabled
remediation: Optional post-Genesis label integration preserving raw addresses and public-data boundaries.
findings.blocking_rationale: Explicitly optional in the dedicated Explorer Genesis profile.

findings.title: Verified-source presentation integration is not established
findings.description: Explorer currently presents runtime code/code hash but does not provide a 420 Verify-backed verified-source/ABI presentation workflow.
evidence: EXP-CAP-015 keeps Explorer's own verdict engine out of scope; EXP-DEP-011 marks Verify metadata optional.
findings.root_cause: Source verification is owned by the separate 420 Verify application and is not required for raw Explorer contract inspection.
consequences: Users must use the owning verification service for reproducible source-verification verdicts.
prerequisite_work: qualified Verify metadata/public interface if later displayed
remediation: Optionally surface verified-source metadata while preserving runtime bytecode as authority and linking to the owning verifier.
findings.blocking_rationale: The Explorer profile treats verified-source data as presentation metadata and does not require Explorer to own verification.

rules.no_speculative_blockers: A finding may be Genesis-blocking only when grounded in an agreed required capability/workflow/dependency, an explicit final-scope decision requirement, or an explicit Genesis operational acceptance criterion.
rules.optional_features: Optional display enrichments and post-Genesis features must not block core Genesis qualification.
rules.unverified_not_failed: Missing runtime evidence is classified as unverified/qualification or operational gap rather than a demonstrated implementation failure unless source evidence proves the capability absent.
